welcome.title: How much time would your household have if income stopped?
welcome.description: Household Runway turns the numbers you know today into an explainable interruption plan. No account required.

location.title: Where does your household live?
location.description: We use your country and region only to estimate take-home pay and show relevant planning reminders. We never need your address.

household.title: Who shares the financial load?
household.description: This is about shared responsibilities, not marital status.

employment.title: What is the household's situation today?
employment.description: Your current reality determines which interruption scenarios are useful.

myIncome.title: What income reaches the household from your work?
myIncome.description: Use take-home pay if you know it. If you enter gross pay, we will show an editable estimate.

partnerIncome.title: What income reaches the household from your partner's work?
partnerIncome.description: We will never ask an unemployed person to enter their old salary.

otherIncome.title: Does dependable income continue outside work?
otherIncome.description: Include only income you can reasonably count on, such as net rent or support. Leave uncertain side work out.

cash.title: How much could pay a bill today?
cash.description: Count cash, checking, and savings that are already available.

confirmedFunds.title: Is any confirmed money on its way?
confirmedFunds.description: Only include money that is confirmed but has not arrived yet. You can skip this.

assets.title: What else does the household own?
assets.description: We separate accessible investments from retirement accounts and home equity so nothing is silently treated as cash.

expenses.title: What would the household still need to pay?
expenses.description: Enter today's spending and the amount it could realistically fall to after an income interruption.

temporaryIncome.title: Are you already receiving time-limited income?
temporaryIncome.description: For example, unemployment benefits already being paid. Do not include benefits you only might qualify for.

review.title: One honest look before the result
review.description: Estimated and skipped answers remain visible. You can change them after seeing the result.

welcome.private: Private by default. Anonymous answers stay in this browser.
welcome.fast: Core path in about 90 seconds. Details are optional.
welcome.explainable: No score. You can see every number behind the result.

fields.otherIncomeHelp: Net rent, support, or other income that continues even if work stops.
fields.availableCashHelp: Include money already received. Do not include a hoped-for severance payment here.
fields.confirmedHelp: Unconfirmed money belongs in What if, not the main result.
fields.investmentAccess: Portion of investments you would treat as accessible

household.sharedHelp: A partner or another adult shares income or required costs.

income.estimate: Estimated take-home pay — review this against a real pay statement
income.notAsked: There is no need to enter a previous salary. The runway uses the income available today.
income.noPartner: You told us no partner shares the household finances, so there is no second income to enter.

expenses.addDetails: Add category details for a more useful plan

validation.region: Add your state, province, or region to continue.
validation.income: Enter an income amount or update the employment status.
validation.reviewEstimate: Review the take-home estimate before continuing, or enter your actual take-home pay.
validation.expenses: Enter an interruption spending amount greater than zero.

result.primary: Your household could cover essential costs for about {months} months — until {date}.
result.primaryOver: Your household could cover essential costs for more than {months} months under these assumptions.
result.sustainable: Your entered continuing income covers your entered essential expenses.

why.title: Why this result
why.excluded: Assets excluded from the main result

precision.title: Best questions to improve precision
precision.cash: Confirm the cash that could pay a bill today.
precision.takeHome: Replace the take-home estimate with a real pay statement amount.
precision.expenses: Break the quick spending total into its largest required categories.

regionalActions.US: Check your state's unemployment process, health coverage options, and the documents needed before an interruption.
regionalActions.CA: Check your province's employment insurance process, health coverage, and required employment records.
regionalActions.CN: Check local unemployment insurance, social insurance continuity, housing fund access rules, and required employment documents.
regionalActions.TW: Check employment insurance benefits, labor insurance continuity, health coverage, and separation documents.

comparison.title: Three ways to view the same household
comparison.description: The main answer uses your interruption plan. Current lifestyle shows the cost of changing nothing; extreme mode previews retirement with a conservative haircut.
comparison.extremeHelp: Includes 70% of retirement balances. Home equity remains excluded.

whatIf.title: What would give you more time?
whatIf.description: These changes are temporary until you apply them.
whatIf.retirementHelp: Shown at a 30% haircut. Taxes and penalties may differ.

method.title: How this is calculated
method.formula: Each month: opening liquid balance + continuing income + confirmed money arriving that month − interruption expenses.
method.excluded: Retirement accounts and home equity are excluded unless you explicitly preview retirement in extreme mode.
method.disclaimer: Educational scenario estimate only. This is not tax, investment, legal, eligibility, or financial advice.

save.title: Keep your runway current
save.description: The full result is free. Create an account only if you want to save it, compare changes, and return later.
